points.point: Headline least-cost design of 8,500 kWp PV is not buildable on the stated land: it needs 9.8 ha versus 9.0 ha set aside, exceeding the 7,830 kWp that fits; the land-constrained alternative is 7,750 kWp at 0.279 USD/kWh.

The 0.277 USD/kWh headline assumes diesel is off for 7,680 h/yr; with a reserve diesel unit always on, the same design costs 0.533 USD/kWh and the reserve-case optimum falls to 49.3% renewable share, so the saving depends on unproven no-diesel grid operation.

A basic plant fact is unresolved: diesel units are modelled as 1800.0 kW although sources also print 2,700 kW; the alternative changes diesel-only LCOE from 0.511 to 0.594 USD/kWh and pushes the least-cost PV size to 9,000 kWp on the search-grid edge.

Weather uncertainty materially changes the optimum: GHI ranges from 1,731 to 2,049 kWh/m2/yr (18.4% spread), with least-cost PV from 7,250 to 8,500 kWp and LCOE from 0.233 to 0.277 USD/kWh depending on source.

Fuel price 1.26 USD/L is explicitly a pre-tax, pre-sea-transport depot floor, with source values ranging 1.03 to 1.64 USD/L; delivered island fuel cost therefore is not established for the 0.511 USD/kWh diesel baseline or the 0.24 USD/L breakeven claim.

Diesel economics rest on assumed, unvalidated parameters — fuel slope 0.25 L/kWh, intercept 0.08 L/h per kW rated, and diesel O&M 0.03 USD/kWh with capital treated as sunk — and no sensitivity tests these assumptions despite diesel-only fuel of 3,653,468 L/yr driving the comparison.

Up-front capital of 18,489,000 USD uses generic prices such as PV capex 1119.0 USD/kWp and battery capex 390.0 USD/kWh, while island shipping, local labour and construction are excluded; remote-island delivered and installed cost is therefore unpriced.

Battery duty is severe at 263 cycles/yr over a 20-year project with a 15-year battery life, yet degradation beyond a replacement rule and salt-air corrosion are excluded from the 0.277 USD/kWh result.

Demand basis needs reconciliation: 9,568,110 kWh/yr with peak 1,422 kW implies a 76.8% load factor, while the underlying Hiron 2021 checks flag an impossible PV yield of 4,291 kWh/kWp, battery output exceeding input, and inconsistent totals; no section explains which Hiron values remain trustworthy for load and plant sizing.

Reported reliability is only hourly energy balance with 0 kWh/yr unserved against an allowed unserved fraction of 0.001; the study does not model forced outages, N-1 loss of the largest diesel or battery inverter, diesel start costs or minimum up/down times, or sub-hourly ramps despite 163 starts/yr in the least-cost design.
